info.title: Mycelium Forge HTTP API
info.description: The Forge registry's HTTP API. Every response body is a flat JSON array; every element is {"@id": ..., "@type": ..., ...own properties}; relationships are never inlined, only {"@id": ..., "@type": ...} stubs. The route surface follows the model's own containment structure (Mycelium.Forge.Generator.Generators.UmlCoreOpenApiPathsGenerator), not REST convention - this API is not meant for humans navigating URLs in a browser. Authorization is out of scope for this document - no operation assumes or encodes an authorization rule; every route is shown as though the caller may do everything shown.

IncludeContained.name: include-contained
IncludeContained.description: Depth of the breadth-first walk over composite/containment edges (IProperty.IsComposite) from the response's root entity/entities. Contained objects are added as additional sibling nodes in the response array, never inlined.

IncludeReferenced.name: include-referenced
IncludeReferenced.description: Depth of the breadth-first walk over plain association edges from the response's root entity/entities. Referenced objects are added as additional sibling nodes in the response array, never inlined.

Identifier.name: identifier
Identifier.description: Every resource is addressed by this same {identifier} segment, in one of three forms - all resolving the same item(s), none more canonical than another. Accepted for GET, PATCH and DELETE unless noted: (1) the resource's own Thing.Id, a canonical GUID (e.g. "3fa85f64-5717-4562-b3fc-2c963f66afa6"); (2) a ShortGuid - a reversible, URL-safe base64 encoding of that same GUID, 22 characters (e.g. "ZF-oPxdXYkWz_CyWP2avpg" for the GUID above); (3) GET only - a bracketed, comma-separated list of ShortGuids (e.g. "[ZF-oPxdXYkWz_CyWP2avpg,...]") for a batch lookup of more than one resource in a single request. The three forms are indistinguishable as OpenAPI path templates (same single-segment shape) - Mycelium.Forge.RouteConstraints disambiguates them at the actual ASP.NET routing layer, each form its own registered route. Not yet implemented: the encode/decode logic itself, and whether a batch PATCH/DELETE (one shared partial body, or removing more than one resource at once) will ever be supported - GET is the only verb the batch form is routed for today.

PartialThing.description: Not yet decided: JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7396) vs JSON Patch (RFC 6902), which properties are patchable, and how this reconciles with the generated schemas' own "every property required" shape (correct for a full GET representation, not for a partial update).

ThingArray.description: A flat array of {"@id", "@type", ...own properties} objects - one element for a single-resource operation, many for anything that returns more.

BadRequest.description: The request could not be understood or failed validation.

NotFound.description: No such resource - or, for a read of a resource the caller isn't authorised to see, the same response as one that doesn't exist (design.md §10.1).

Conflict.description: The request conflicts with the resource's current state (e.g. a delete blocked by a foreign-key reference still pointing at it).

NotAcceptable.description: The Accept header names a media type/schema version this Forge instance doesn't support (design.md §10.3). Never silently falls back to the latest version.

ProblemDetails.description: RFC 9457 Problem Details, plus a correlationId extension member (design.md §10.1) so a user-facing error can quote it.

type.description: Defaults to "about:blank" when no more specific URI is registered.
